clue.text: Song about a primal curse

indicators.note: about means the word for a song wraps round the next piece

parts.note: an anthem is a song of praise or loyalty
primal means first, and A is first in the alphabet, as in A1

explanation.surface: A ballad tells of the original curse laid on mankind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside ANTHEM to give ANATHEM; a second A, from 'primal', completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: An anathema is a formal ecclesiastical curse or denunciation, hence a curse generally.

clue.text: Insured a flat built by contributor to the 13

indicators.note: built means the letters are assembled into a new structure

explanation.surface: Someone insured a flat that was put up by an anthology contributor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'built' rearranges INSURED A FLAT. Alfred Austin was a Poet Laureate famously mocked for poor verse, so he appears in The Stuffed Owl, the anthology of bad verse at 13.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Austin's verses were collected in The Stuffed Owl, an anthology of bad poetry, making him a contributor.

clue.text: See 1 down
Climber said to be a legal term

indicators.note: said means the clue's word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: Edmund Hillary was the mountaineer who first climbed Everest with Tenzing

explanation.surface: A mountaineer is reported to be a piece of legal jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Term' looks like a word or expression, but the Hilary term is a sitting of the English courts and Oxford's spring term.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hilary sittings are one of the four periods of the English legal year, named after St Hilary.

clue.text: General Medical Council at sea over an abrasion in writer of 8

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of the council's abbreviation are jumbled

parts.note: GMC is the abbreviation for the UK's General Medical Council, which registers doctors
over means on, as in on top of or concerning
the indefinite article an can be shortened to A
a gall is a sore made by rubbing, an abrasion

explanation.surface: Doctors' regulatory body, adrift, has a graze in a bad poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' scrambles GMC into MCG. William McGonagall, the Dundee poet, is renowned as the worst poet in English.
explanation.definitionFit: William McGonagall is famous for some of the most comically dreadful verse in the language, the bad verse of 8.

clue.text: Light blue marker on container

indicators.note: on here means the marker word comes after the container word

parts.note: a can is a container such as a tin
a tab is a small marker or label

explanation.surface: A pale blue label is stuck on a tin.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge University's colour is light blue, so a Cantab (a Cambridge man or woman) is a Light Blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantab, short for Cantabrigian, denotes Cambridge, whose sporting colour is light blue.

clue.text: Place for Petruchio's greeting to his wife, say?

indicators.note: say means the phrase is spoken aloud

parts.note: Petruchio marries Kate in The Taming of the Shrew, so he might greet her with a casual 'allo, Kate

explanation.surface: Asks where Shakespeare's Petruchio would greet his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' is a verb here, meaning assign or apportion.
explanation.definitionFit: To place something can mean to assign or apportion it, as a sense of allot or assign.

clue.text: Numbers eating big apple take on prestigious contributor to the 13

indicators.note: eating means the numbers word swallows the next piece

parts.note: tens are numbers
the Big Apple is New York, abbreviated NY
taken as written

explanation.surface: Figures consuming New York take on a famous poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take' is a link. Even the great Tennyson has lines in The Stuffed Owl, hence 'prestigious'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Tennyson, Poet Laureate, had some weaker lines included in The Stuffed Owl anthology of bad verse.

clue.text: Initiator of balladry? On the contrary, doggerel, collected in …

indicators.note: initiator of means the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: adverse means contrary, opposed

explanation.surface: The start of a ballad, the opposite in fact: shoddy rhyme gathered in an anthology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' looks like a linking phrase but gives ADVERSE; 'collected in …' leads on to 13, The Stuffed Owl.
explanation.definitionFit: Doggerel is crude, badly made poetry, which is exactly what poor verse means.

clue.text: Blend some beer with body in aircraft

parts.note: to fuse is to blend or melt together

indicators.note: some means only part of the beer word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: lager is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Mixing some beer with the body of a plane.
explanation.definitionFit: The fuselage is the main central body of an aeroplane, holding crew and passengers.

clue.text: Reproduced on its own in means of reproduction

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a CD, compact disc, is a means of reproducing recorded sound
lone means solitary, on its own

explanation.surface: Something copied by itself inside a reproductive system.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means of reproduction' suggests biology, but it is a compact disc.
explanation.definitionFit: To clone is to make a genetically identical copy, so cloned means reproduced exactly.

clue.text: I leave the country half topless with allowance

indicators.note: topless means the first letter is removed from the word for half

parts.note: hemi- is a prefix meaning half
a grant is an allowance of money

explanation.surface: Someone half-naked with a stipend announces they are going abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks as the emigrant: 'I leave the country' describes oneself as one.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant is a person who leaves their own country to settle in another.

clue.text: Reproduction of number in Jaguar

indicators.note: in means the number goes inside the car model

parts.note: the E-type is a classic Jaguar sports car
C is the Roman numeral for 100

explanation.surface: A copy of a numbered Jaguar car.
explanation.definitionFit: An ectype is a copy or reproduction, as opposed to the original prototype.

clue.text: … taxidermist's "Wisdom", formed of dust few left off

indicators.note: formed means the letters are shaped into something new

parts.note: left gives its abbreviation L, with off rounding out the phrase as in left off the list

explanation.surface: A preserved bird made of dust, with few remaining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'formed' scrambles OF DUST FEW plus L. The owl symbolises wisdom; The Stuffed Owl is also a 1930 anthology of bad verse, the 13 the other clues refer to.
explanation.definitionFit: The owl is the emblem of wisdom, so a preserved, mounted one is wisdom as a taxidermist renders it.

clue.text: To sit again may cause ripples

indicators.note: may cause signals that the fodder letters can produce a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Sitting down again might stir up waves.
explanation.definitionFit: Agitations of a water surface are ripples or disturbances, a synonym in the physical sense.

clue.text: Cured itch to bring up food: marmalade's best, they say

indicators.note: cured means treated or processed, so the letters are reworked
to bring up, in a down clue, reads the food word from bottom to top

parts.note: tuck is British slang for food, especially schoolchildren's snacks

explanation.surface: Treating an itch to bring food back up: the best marmalade, reportedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cured' scrambles ITCH into THIC; 'to bring up' turns TUCK into KCUT. 'they say' marks the definition as popular opinion, not a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Thick-cut marmalade, with chunky peel, is held by many to be the finest kind.

clue.text: Tale about invalid being resurrected is likely to be wrong

indicators.note: about means the tale word goes round the next piece

parts.note: a fable is a tale

indicators.note: being resurrected means raised up, so in a down clue the word is read upwards

parts.note: ill describes an invalid, someone sick

explanation.surface: A story about a sick person rising from the dead is probably false.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'being resurrected' means raised, so the sick word is read upwards before going inside the story.
explanation.definitionFit: Fallible means capable of making mistakes, so liable to be in error.

clue.text: Revolutionary with links to the East turning up has to scarper

parts.note: Che Guevara is the archetypal revolutionary
E is the abbreviation for East

indicators.note: turning up, in a down clue, reads the links word from bottom to top

parts.note: ties are links or bonds

explanation.surface: A revolutionary with Eastern connections who turns up must run away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses TIES to SEIT. 'Cheese it' is dated slang for 'run off!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese it is old slang telling someone to make off quickly, the same as scarper.

clue.text: Novel hero finds open ground on mountainside

parts.note: a heath is open uncultivated ground
a cliff is a steep rock face on a mountainside

explanation.surface: A fictional protagonist discovers moorland on a mountain slope.
explanation.walkthrough: Heathcliff is the hero of Emily Brontë's Wuthering Heights, set on the Yorkshire moors.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathcliff is the central brooding figure of the novel Wuthering Heights.

clue.text: Damage to colour by superior contributor to the 13

parts.note: to mar is to damage or spoil
a tint is a colour
upper means higher, superior

explanation.surface: Spoiling paint by a better poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'by' are links. Martin Tupper's Proverbial Philosophy was hugely popular but is now a byword for platitude.
explanation.definitionFit: Martin Tupper's moralising verse earned him a place in The Stuffed Owl anthology of bad poetry.

clue.text: See 19
Very soft-hearted footballer's stone

indicators.note: hearted means the soft piece is placed in the heart of the footballer's name

parts.note: Pelé is the great Brazilian footballer
BB marks a very soft pencil lead

explanation.surface: A tender-hearted footballer owns a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'soft-hearted' looks like kindness, but splits into a pencil grade and an insertion signal; Pelé is the Brazilian forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A pebble is a small smooth stone, worn round by water.

clue.text: Spooner's foolish friend, contributor to the 13

indicators.note: Spooner's means the opening sounds of two words are swapped

parts.note: silly means foolish
cobber is Australian slang for a friend or mate

explanation.surface: A Spoonerism about a daft mate who contributed to an anthology.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of SILLY COBBER gives 'Colly Sibber'. Colley Cibber was an 18th-century Poet Laureate mocked by Pope.
explanation.definitionFit: Colley Cibber, a much-derided Poet Laureate, has verses in The Stuffed Owl anthology of bad poetry.

clue.text: Spoil a set outside

indicators.note: outside means the set word goes round the a

parts.note: a denture is a set of false teeth

explanation.surface: Ruin a stage set from the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' suggests scenery, but it is a set of false teeth.
explanation.definitionFit: To denature something is to change its natural qualities, spoiling it, as with denatured alcohol.

clue.text: See 22
Linklater's hostelry for many in this puzzle?

definitions.text: Linklater's hostelry for many in this puzzle?

parts.words: Linklater's hostelry for many in this puzzle?
parts.note: Eric Linklater wrote a 1929 comic novel named after an inn, and the puzzle is full of versifiers who might drink in one

explanation.surface: Asks which inn a Scottish novelist named that suits the rhymers in this crossword.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Linklater's novel takes its title from a tavern for versifiers, which suits this puzzle's many rhymers.

clue.text: Score that went your way in part

indicators.note: in part means the answer is a portion of these words

explanation.surface: A tally that came your way in part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way' is padding for the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, the old counting unit.

clue.text: Swanning around for something to eat on lake

parts.note: a flan is an open tart, something to eat
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Idling about for a tart beside a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'on' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Flânerie, from French, is aimless idle strolling, much like swanning about.
